mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25 percentage points for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, thereby depressing earnings and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent decline in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index over three months signals a coordinated easing of monetary policy and disinflation, which lowers risk premia and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) combined with a concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand, which expands corporate revenue and profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both increase for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in the Housing Opportunities Price Index (HOUST) below its trough level during the prior recession signals persistent housing market weakness, which drags on construction and related industries and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST remains below prior recession trough for at least 12 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when HOUST remains below prior recession trough for at least 12 months.
